section_1.title: The Hook: The Chaos of Individuals
section_1.content: Begin with a visual of a non-normal distribution (e.g., a 'Uniform' or 'Skewed' distribution). Explain that individual data points are unpredictable, representing noise.
section_1.example: Visualize a group of 100 squirrels jumping distances. Some jump short, some jump long—the distribution of individual jump lengths is totally chaotic (Uniform).

section_2.title: The Prerequisite: Averages as Stabilizers
section_2.content: Introduce the concept of 'Sampling Distribution.' Explain that when we take the *average* of a sample, we are performing a mathematical smoothing process that reduces the noise of individual extremes.
section_2.example: Instead of tracking one squirrel, we track the *average* jump distance of a group of 10 squirrels. We repeat this 1,000 times.

section_3.title: The Reveal: Convergence to the Bell Curve
section_3.content: Visually demonstrate the transformation. As sample size (n) increases, the chaotic distribution morphs into a perfect Normal Distribution (the 'Bell Curve'). This is the CLT in action.
section_3.example: Show an animation of the 'chaotic' squirrel graph collapsing into a smooth, symmetrical Bell Curve as the group size increases from 2 to 30.

section_4.title: Key Properties & Constraints
section_4.content: Summarize the three critical takeaways: 1. The mean of sample means equals the population mean. 2. The variance decreases as sample size grows. 3. It works regardless of the original distribution (as long as it's independent).
section_4.example: A visual 'Math Cheat Sheet' overlaying the screen: μ_x̄ = μ, σ_x̄ = σ/√n.

section_5.title: Application: Predicting the Future
section_5.content: Explain why this matters: It allows us to make confident predictions about large groups (e.g., polling, quality control) even if we don't know the underlying individual behavior.
section_5.example: A quality control robot in a cookie factory: It doesn't know the weight of one single chocolate chip, but because of CLT, it can guarantee the average weight of a bag of 50 cookies will stay within a precise, predictable range.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(f"- {line}", font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                # Shift right to give room for lecture
                x = 2.5 + j * 0.8
                y = 2.0 - i * 0.8
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Hook: The Chaos of Individuals", [
            "Individual data points are often chaotic and unpredictable.",
            "Consider a uniform distribution of squirrel jumps.",
            "There is no clear pattern in the noise."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Create scatter plot of 100 points
        np.random.seed(42)
        dots = VGroup(*[Dot(color="#FF9900", radius=0.05) for _ in range(100)])
        for dot in dots:
            dot.move_to(np.array([np.random.uniform(-2, 2), np.random.uniform(-1, 1), 0]))
        
        scatter = self.place_in_area(dots, "B1", "E6", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(FadeIn(dots))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FF9900")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        label = Text("Uniform Distribution: Individual Squirrels", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(label, "A3", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Write(label))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF9900")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(Indicate(dots, color="#FF9900"))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF9900")
        self.wait(2)

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Key Properties & Constraints", [
            "Mean of sample means equals population mean.",
            "Variance decreases as sample size grows.",
            "Independence is essential for this convergence."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        formula_mean = MathTex(r"\mu_{\bar{x}}", "=", r"\mu", color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(formula_mean, 'B2', 'B5', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Write(formula_mean))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        formula_var = MathTex(r"\sigma_{\bar{x}}", "=", r"\frac{\sigma}{\sqrt{n}}", color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(formula_var, 'C2', 'C5', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Write(formula_var))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GREEN))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        indep_text = Text("Independence Required", font_size=32, color=YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(indep_text, 'D3', scale_factor=0.9)
        
        bell = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/bell.svg")
        self.place_at_grid(bell, 'E3', scale_factor=0.5)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(indep_text), FadeIn(bell))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        # Bell curve narrowing animation
        self.play(bell.animate.scale(0.5), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(2)
